message.content:
The sea can look like a spectrum of colors depending on a few factors:

| Factor | Typical Color |
|--------|---------------|
| **Depth** | Deeper water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) and reflects shorter wavelengths (blue, green). So deep ocean water often looks a deep blue or even indigo. |
| **Sunlight angle** | At sunrise/sunset the sea can take on warm hues—golden, pink, or orange—because the light passes through more atmosphere. |
| **Algae & phytoplankton** | In shallower, nutrient‑rich waters, microscopic plants give the water a greenish tint. |
| **Sediment & clarity** | Turbid or sandy waters can appear brownish or muddy. |
| **Ice & snow** | Near polar regions, the sea can look almost white or pale blue due to ice crystals and reflected sunlight. |

So, while the “color of the sea” is often described as blue, it can actually range from turquoise and green to deep indigo, and even warm hues near shorelines or during sunrise/sunset.
